context: 041122's cell pitch was measured, not reasoned about, and the carry-over's number is wrong: the verification cell's source baselines are 12.000 pt apart and the writer already emits w:line=240 tw for them, so the '232 not 240' change would compress every line of that cell. The row's declared trHeight (4630 tw = 231.5 pt) and its content (232 pt) agree to 0.5 pt; the '11.6 pt pitch' was 4630 divided by the rendered line count. What is left on this class is a WRAP: each of that cell's paragraphs takes 12/24/24/24 pt in the render instead of a flat 12, so the cantSplit row is pushed whole to the next page and 041122 renders 11-12 pages against the source's 9. The font is a contributing cause but NOT the mechanism: extracting the source's embedded Effra subsets, rewriting their name tables with fonttools so fontconfig binds them, and re-rendering puts pages 8-10 in Effra-Medium/Effra-Bold and the document still renders 12 pages with item 22b on page 9, exactly as with Noto Sans. Measured for the next run: our cell's right rule is at x 572.9, the source's longest line ends at 569.0 - 3.9 pt of slack - so the next question is whether that 3.9 pt is our cell width or our run metrics, not the writer's line box. A debug probe was added to DocxWriter this run (-Dp2w.dbgCells=1) and is off by default; it is what produced this evidence. The stale NEEDS-A-HUMAN entry that blamed a permission for subagents' commits was cleared: git push is 403 for everyone and the GitHub MCP contents API is the tool, exactly as the operator note says.
